message.content:
The total number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess (ignoring the “legal‑ness” constraint) is astronomically large – roughly on the order of **10⁴⁶**.  

In more detail:

| Category | Rough estimate |
|----------|----------------|
| All possible placements of the 32 pieces (including illegal ones) | ≈ 10⁴⁶ |
| Legal positions only (respecting rules such as no two kings in check, correct castling rights, etc.) | ≈ 10⁴³ |

So when people talk about the “Shannon number” for chess, they’re usually referring to the number of possible games (~10¹²⁰), but the sheer number of possible board arrangements is about 10⁴⁶.
